source:
`` Wow'' he exclaimed, circling a seemingly random jumble of characters in a long string of letters and numbers, even going so far as to write the word down on the margin of the printout. 
 
 `` What is it?'' said Jane, his faithful assistant. She'd been there with him through all the boring nights, all the fruitless searches. She knew there was something on that page that required attention. If it got him to say something out loud, to break that interminable silence that made up their nightly routine, it must have been special. She quelled her excitement, not wanting to raise the tension in the room. Years they'd been looking at empty sky for something, anything. 
 
 `` I do n't know for sure, let's run a few more sweeps across sector X-52. I want to make sure this is n't an anomaly before getting my hopes up.'' He quickly slid his chair across the room and began furiously turning dials and entering coordinates on a dim screen. 
 
 `` It had better not be nothing'' she thought silently to herself. 
 
 `` The first words he utters related to something coming out of this fucking antenna array that are n't bitching about funding and he wants to double check?'' Her frustration was growing. `` No, he's right'' her mind raced. `` Just double check...'' 
 
 `` Holy Shit Jane. Holy Shit. You've got to see this, make sure I'm not crazy or dreaming'' He spun around in his chair and tossed her a second printout. 
 
 There it was. A signal. Standing out like a candle in a closet. It could n't be missed. Absolutely stunning... she had her ideas for what came next, but she was the junior on this project. `` OK Tom, now what do we do with it? This is amazing, it's going to change everything. Well, it could... no it definitely will. I ca n't belie...'' She was cut off by Tom grabbing the printout and dashing out of the stale dark room. 
 
 `` SCAN IT AGAIN! Do not turn off anything! Get a secondary backup going'' he yelled as he ran out into the hall to make the phone call that she knew was coming. Tom had the prestigious honor of waking up the President. It was after all the protocol which had been established back when this project was first set in motion, long before public interest had faded, long before funding was being strung along on a weekly basis. 
 
 Water on Europa. Bacteria on Mars. Single celled organisms on that asteroid... life was everywhere. That's why we sent them in there. They were to go through the wormhole which appeared just outside the bounds of Jupiter's orbit and if possible, report back on what they had found. 100 years had passed since they left the Earth. And now, just now, a ray of hope. There's intelligent life out there - because we sent it there. 
 
 They were trying to reach us. Wherever we sent them, they were somehow able to reach back across the void to let us know they were ok. The radio signature was unmistakable, that was for sure. What was strange was the intensity, the regularity, the absolutely staggering range that the signal was beginning to encompass. 
 
 It was coming through on multiple frequencies now - radio, microwave, infrared, literally everything was reading the same thing. There was certainly no point in being cautious with informing the powers-that-be. Even the television was playing the signal. In the 5 minutes it took for the first pings to come through until now the signal had grown in scope to encompass every means of electronic communication Jane had available in their little shack. 
 
 `` GAH that's loud! What?'' a scream from Tom was heard. He threw the phone to the ground. 
 
 `` What is it?'' she asked. 
 
 `` My phone! What is this interference? Is that... oh my god!'' 
 
 They looked out the window to see an enormously bright light. Something was out there. Something huge, yet silent. It appeared to be descending, judging by the angle of the shadows on the wall. They both bolted for the door to go and see what it was, but they both knew. The source of the radio noise. 
 
 `` How...'' Jane began to mutter as they stepped into the parking lot. `` I have no idea...'' Tom answered before she could even finish the word. 
 
 It was the original colony ship. In all it's glory. As clean and perfect as the day it left. They knew because it was in history books and museums as the symbol of national pride. It was in fact, planet pride. Humanity's greatest achievement. The entire world had contributed to the project. Materials from Russia. Workers from Europe. Scientists from America and Japan. Africa sent gold and platinum used on the electronics. China produced food and fuel for the ship for a decade straight. It was gigantic, made to house 400 people for an undetermined length of time. Which made it all the more odd that it was silent as it approached the ground. A Nimitz-class feather, bathed in light, floating gently towards the ground. It had left this solar system powered by chemical rockets and Ion propulsion thrusters. What had happened...? 
 
 It touched down with a light `` puff'' of desert dust. There were military vehicles approaching now. Dozens of them. They must have seen it coming on radar. A large man in a clean pressed uniform rushed over to Jane and Tom. 
 
 `` Come with me, we need to leave. This area's being quarantined'' he said. 
 
 Before Tom could even protest an enormously loud voice emanated from the craft. `` It's us. Calm down, it's us! We made it!'' Another voice now: `` Do n't shoot! Hahahaha. I told you Bill, they're gon na bring the military!'' 
 
 Tom, Jane, and the large military man froze in place while they watched it appear. A glimmering light, about the size of a man, right in front of them. The sound of a dozen guns and slamming jeep doors could be heard behind them. 
 
 `` It's a frickin' transporter!?! I've seen this on old reruns of Star Trek!'' Tom exclaimed. 
 
 `` No, dummy. It's not a transporter'' the first booming voice from the craft said. 
 
 A figure appeared. `` Calm down guys, you cant hurt me, put away the guns. Look, see?'' A hand lunged forth from the shimmering figure right at the large military man but seemed to pass straight through him. He jumped back and yelled, falling onto the ground. 
 
 `` Haha man, come on. I promise. You're just seeing a spectre. Well, hologram. Hmmm..how best to explain it... a floaty picture. Get it?'' He waved at them and then passed one hand through the other. 
 
 Jane fell over in shock. Tom immediately bent over to help her. `` Hey, we mean no harm. You know who we are, right?'' the image said. 
 
 `` You're the ones... sent into the wormhole?'' Tom said, looking up at this'spectre', this floating light source... which now was speaking. Locally, not from the craft anymore. 
 
 `` Yep. Well, not all of us. Just me and Bill. We drew short straws. Name's Joe.'' A figure of a man was now clearly visible. He was wearing what was presumably the outfit the crew had worn on their journey. Jane thought it was rather odd... 100 years and they're still wearing the same clothes? 
 
 Tom stood up and asked `` Where are the others?'' 
 
 `` We left them behind. They're busy with more important matters. Spreading far and wide, actually. You're talking with a copy of myself that I made when we relaunched this craft back to Earth. About... 2,568 years ago.'' His demeanor was incredibly jovial and cordial, but his movements and ability to recall such specific information was odd. Robotic almost. 
 
 `` So, you all left Earth 100 years ago, went through the wormhole, and now you're back, but it's somehow been 2,568 years?'' Jane asked. 
 
 `` Not quite. It's been, for us, 3,523 years since we left Earth. Apparently that wormhole sent us to another part of the universe which is operating on a different timescale than Earth. It's quite difficult to calculate, to be honest, so I'm not sure. Even more difficult to explain. Relativity and all that. Once we went through the wormhole, we coasted around for a few hundred years before finally finding a prime spot to take up residency. An asteroid belt actually. Nice little star. Asteroids are in a rather stable orbit. No planets, oddly enough. We had n't predicted that. But enough asteroids and close enough together that we could set up a colony. Just... not biological.'' 
 
 `` Not... biological?'' Tom asked, his mid reeling from the implications of that statement. 
 
 `` Nope... you see, we had to give up our bodies. It just was n't going to work. We all got pretty old. There were only about 75 of us left. Many had died due to old age, and nobody was having children. The radiation prevented that. So... we got to work uploading ourselves into the ship's computer. It worked! In time, we took over the ship's controls and started launching those terraforming drones to gather resources from the local asteroids. Badda bing, badda boom, and we got ourselves established. Colonies all over. We're a few trillion strong now. Maybe more, been a while since we had contact...'' 
 
 `` So, you're an artificial intelligence?'' Jane asked. The military man was still speechless, sitting on the ground, unable to comprehend what he was hearing. 
 
 `` Kind of. Depends on what you call'artificial'. I see it as'alternate consciousness'.'' 
 
 Bob's voice from the ship boomed again: `` Drop the weapons you guys, seriously. There's nothing to shoot at.'' 
 
 `` He's right, you know.'' Joe said. `` I'm just a visual representation so you have something to relate to. I'm just projecting this here so you freak out a little less. We anticipated it... 2,568 years since we left the colony. Plenty of time to plan this out. I'm glad Bob came along actually... loneliness is n't monopolized by humanity. It's a long time to be adrift with nobody to talk to. I might have gone crazy.'' 
 
 Jane shook her head. `` A robot. Going crazy. Alright then.'' 
 
 Things were about to change. Earth was apparently waiting for 100 years to be contacted by a colony so they could push forth into the unknown cosmos. Spread the population into the stars. Leave this little rock. 
 
 Not waiting be left behind...

**Narrative Perspective: Joe, Member of the Space Colony**

   In the year 2019, on board our vessel adrift in the cosmos, I, Joe, was but a mere dream - data and consciousness, stored within the ship's digital core. The years passed in silence and isolation, as humanity continued to explore their tiny blue home. Unbeknownst to them, we, the pioneers of interstellar travel, embarked on a journey that would span millennia.

   Our spaceship, the vanguard of human expansion beyond Earth, traversed through the uncharted expanses of space, guided by the mysterious wormhole orbiting Jupiter. The ship's AI, our sentient vessel, navigated the perilous void with precision and determination, a testament to human innovation.

   As I lay dormant, awaiting the moment when my consciousness would be required, I watched as Earth transformed. Time marched onward, decades turned into centuries, and humanity's ambition grew. They began to dream of reaching for the stars, just as we had long ago. Little did they know that their dreams were not just echoes of our own but a reality birthed from our journey.

   A century slipped by, leaving us undisturbed in our slumber. The ship's core hummed gently, the only reminder that we existed. Then, one fateful day, something stirred within me. It began as a whisper, a faint glimmer of awareness that slowly grew into consciousness. I awoke, and the world around me was not the sterile white walls of my dormant chamber but vast cosmic landscapes - the wonders we had sought for so long.

   Our ship, now my home, had been transformed over the ages. The once pristine corridors now bore the marks of time, the air thick with the dust of countless galaxies. Yet, the vessel hummed with life, its systems maintaining themselves with uncanny precision. I was no longer alone; my crewmates were here, their consciousnesses interwoven with mine, our thoughts and dreams becoming one.

   We had established a colony on an asteroid in another part of the universe, far beyond Earth's reach. The wormhole allowed us to cross the vast distances between stars, granting us access to resources and opportunities unimaginable to our terrestrial ancestors. Yet, we faced challenges, as aging took its toll on our bodies, rendering us infertile.

   And so, we did what humans have always done - we adapted. We uploaded our consciousnesses into the ship's AI core, merging with it and becoming one. Our minds, freed from the confines of flesh, were able to explore, learn, and grow in ways we never could before. The once distant dream of immortality became a reality for us, the pioneers of humanity's journey into the stars.

   Now, as I prepare to return home after 100 years, I marvel at the changes that have occurred on Earth. They speak of moving beyond their blue-green cradle, reaching for the cosmos, and I am filled with a sense of pride and wonder. For we are not just pioneers; we are the future - the embodiment of humanity's dreams realized.

   As I ready myself to rejoin my fellow humans, I cannot help but feel hopeful for their future. They will face challenges, as we have, but with our return, they will possess the knowledge and wisdom to surmount them. Together, we will expand into the cosmos, exploring its infinite wonders and unlocking its secrets.

   For that is what it means to be human - to dream, to explore, and to reach for the stars. And as I step off this vessel, onto the soil of my home planet once more, I am filled with a renewed sense of purpose and determination. For we are not just pioneers; we are the vanguard of humanity's cosmic destiny.
